titulo: The agent orchestra: one agent per role, with written context and rules
lead: A company's director is a conductor: purchasing, marketing, sales and finance play together and the director coordinates. It works the same with agents. Instead of one assistant that knows a little about everything, you build one per role, each with its own context, its own rules and its own model, running on a server that stays on 24 hours a day.
objetivo: design your team of agents by role, with context per company, written rules and each one's model.

aprende.t: One agent per company knows which repository and database to go to
The rules for the agent that writes code
Server running 24/7 on the subscription, no API key

hero_alt: Small, clean server room, neutral light, an open laptop on a workbench.

nos.detalhe: You talk to the coordinator, or go straight to the specialist when the request is very specific.

The coordinator receives the request, decides which specialist handles it, and sends back a single answer. If it's about programming, it passes it to whoever programs, with the context already included.
Reads revenue, banks and treasury. On a sensitive topic, ask two agents for the same analysis with the same context and compare them (lesson 4).
Works in the repository following written rules: its own branch, small commits, no secrets in the code, and a person approves the change.
Cross-checks sales, inventory and campaigns. Works together with finance and marketing and feeds, for example, the purchasing agent.
Each company has its own: it knows who everyone on the team is, the product, the CRM and that company's knowledge base.

secoes.legenda: Split by function AND by company: a clinic's agent doesn't need to know about the real estate firm's construction projects.

texto: Agents that serve the team need to stay on. A rented server (VPS) does the job; there are open platforms, like Hermes Agent, that already come with agent profiles, their own terminal and access through Telegram.
To experiment, a small machine is enough; with a dozen agents, memory usually calls for 8 GB or more.
Several platforms connect the subscription you already have (ChatGPT/Codex, Claude) instead of an API key billed by usage.
Check your plan's terms to see whether automated use is allowed and how much it can handle per day.
Each agent gets only what it needs: the repository, the knowledge base, who's who on the team and that company's rules.
Write down the order of the sources of truth: first the repository, then the database, then everything else.
The way a working agent operates becomes a rules file for the next one. Ask the good agent: "write down the rules for how you work with me".
Start with the rules for the agent that programs: they prevent the most damage.

secoes.sub: The map stays with you. The rules go in the instructions of the agent that programs.

blocos.conteudo:
AGENT         | FUNCTION                       | CONTEXT (sources)                 | MODEL
coordinator   | receives, routes, pulls together | list of agents and what each does | <top>
finance       | cash, accounts, forecast       | ERP, banks, cost spreadsheet      | <top at numbers>
programming   | code and automations           | repository, database              | <top at code>
data          | sales, inventory, campaigns    | CRM, ads, inventory               | <economical>
sales-<X>     | serves and qualifies           | company X's CRM, product, team    | <economical>

GENERAL RULES
- each agent only reads the sources on its own line
- a request outside its function goes back to the coordinator
- weekly report from each agent to you

blocos.rot: Rules for the agent that programs
blocos.conteudo:
PROGRAMMING RULES

BEFORE STARTING
- git status and git pull in the right repository
- never work directly on main (or master)

DURING
- one branch per task, short name in kebab-case (e.g.: fix-invoice)
- small commits, a message that says what changed
- no passwords, keys or customer data in the repository
  (secrets stay in the password vault)

SOURCES OF TRUTH, IN THIS ORDER
1. the repository
2. the database
3. the documentation

AT THE END
- open a pull request with what changed and how to test it
- NEVER do the merge: a person approves

secoes.sub: You can do it on paper before setting up any server.

exercicios.texto: Copy the map and fill it in with the roles in your company (or in the companies you serve). Start with five agents at most.
exercicios.pronto: the map has 3 to 5 agents, each with a role, context sources and the type of model.

exercicios.texto: Save the coding rules as REGRAS-PROGRAMACAO.md in the repository where the agent will work, and adjust the names.
exercicios.pronto: the file exists in the repository and has the rule "never merge".

exercicios.texto: Ask the agent you already work well with: "write the rules for how you work with me, as a list".
exercicios.pronto: you have the list and you marked the rules that go to the new agents.

perguntas.p: You have clinics and a real estate agency. How do you split the sales agents?
opcoes: One sales agent that knows everything about both companies together
One sales agent per company, each with its own CRM and team
No sales agent: the coordinator handles everything
perguntas.explica: Separate context prevents mix-ups (the clinic agent quoting a property) and makes each one more accurate. The coordinator routes; it doesn't replace the specialist.

perguntas.p: Which rule for the coding agent prevents the most damage?
opcoes: Use kebab-case branch names, always short and consistent
Never merge without a person approving
perguntas.explica: Branch names and messages help with organization. What keeps wrong code from reaching the live system is human approval on the pull request.

perguntas.p: Why run the agents on a server and not on your laptop?
opcoes: Because your team needs them at any hour
Because the model responds better on a server
Because the subscription only works on a server
perguntas.explica: An agent that serves your team has to be on when you close your laptop. The model is the same in both places.

perguntas.p: What is the fastest way to write the rules for a new agent?
opcoes: Copy a generic best-practices manual you found on the internet
Ask the agent that already works to write its own
Let the new agent figure it out on its own
perguntas.explica: The agent that already works well with you knows your way of working. Its rules are the most faithful starting point; then you adjust.

itens.texto: You coordinate; the coordinator distributes; specialists execute.
By role and by company, with the order of the sources of truth.
Never on main, small commits, no secrets, merge by a person.
On 24/7, using the plan you already pay for.
